scenes.headline: POMELLI: PRODUCT *PHOTOS*
scenes.say: Pomelli can turn a plain product photo into branded marketing images, without booking a studio.
You give Google's tool your website or brand materials, so it learns your colors, type and visual style.
Then Photoshoot creates studio or lifestyle variations, which you can refine and download.

scenes.heading: ONE BRAND, *MORE ASSETS*
scenes.say: It also makes campaign assets, while its agent features can build brand books and websites from that context.

cons: AI can change labels, colors or shapes
Review every product detail before running an ad
scenes.say: But these are not real photoshoots. AI can change product details, so check labels, colors and shapes before using an image in an ad.

scenes.heading: CHECK YOUR *ACCESS*
scenes.say: Google calls this a free Labs experiment, with availability and languages depending on your region. Useful, but not a reason to skip accuracy.
What product would you shoot first? Comment brand.

youtube.title: Pomelli: Free AI Product Photos—with a Catch
youtube.description:
Pomelli is Google Labs' AI marketing experiment. Photoshoot turns a product image into brand-aware studio/lifestyle variations using Business DNA, and lets you edit/download results. Agent features also support brand books and websites. Google describes it as free; regional/language availability and experiment limits apply. AI may alter your actual product, so check labels, proportions, colors and claims before using an output commercially. This is a current tool spotlight, not a claim of an October launch.
Official sources: https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/google-labs/pomelli-photoshoot/ and https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/google-labs/pomelli-agentic-capabilities/
